key_insight: Ethylenediamine reconstructs tin-rich tin–lead perovskite surfaces, improving electron extraction and reducing interfacial losses to enable 25.86% solar-cell efficiency.
engineering_relevance: Controlling passivant protonation and surface stoichiometry offers a route to more efficient methylammonium-free perovskite solar cells.
method: Compare neutral ethylenediamine with protonated ethylenediammonium iodide surface treatments.
Use atomistic simulations to investigate vacancy-assisted iodide migration and deprotonation.
Link surface reconstruction to electron extraction into C60 and reduced nonradiative recombination.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 25.86% power conversion efficiency and simulations showing that subsurface iodide vacancies lower the energetic cost of deprotonation.
watch_item: Long-term operational stability and scalability of the surface treatment are not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Controlling Surface Chemistry in Tin-Lead Perovskites for High-Efficiency Solar Cells
